scope: Seven-day persistent SOTA compute and terminal-artifact monitor
summary: A detached monitor now audits all configured hosts and three critical long-running jobs every 120 seconds, persists capacity/transitions, and automatically launches the frozen BWM postprocessor after matched generation completes.
evidence: Detached shellId 553 is running independently of the agent session.
The first verified heartbeat reports bwm-wipe20-seed42, droid-heldout-mapping, and curobo-source-transfer as running.
Capacity snapshots classify a GPU as free only below 1 GiB with no compute process.
The monitor writes capacity.jsonl, events.jsonl, heartbeat.json, config provenance, and successor logs under outputs/sota-monitor/20260812T110000Z-long-term-v1.
The BWM successor is a fixed argv command that discovers exactly one official and candidate campaign and runs the 20-independent-episode, 10,000-bootstrap evaluator.
lessons: Long-running transfers and GPU queues require artifact-triggered continuation rather than relying on an interactive SSH/controller connection.
Any unexplained GPU allocation is now reserved, even when enough nominal memory remains for co-scheduling.
limitations: The monitor depends on the local machine and SSH credentials remaining available.
zhaoli remains inaccessible and pro5000 remains unresolved.
Only the BWM terminal event currently has an automatic scientific postprocessor; DROID and Curobo successors remain explicit next actions.
next_actions: Keep the monitor active until all three jobs are terminal, then append their results and stage the next matched experiments.
